text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-The head of Israel's proxy militia in Lebanon General Lahd warned Lebanese leaders of a possible widescale Israeli operation in Lebanon if serious violence flared on the Lebanon-Israel border.
-Parliament Speaker Berri discussed with President Hrawi Lahd's threats.
-U.S. ambassador Jones: Some considerations might lead to the resumption of peace talks between Israel and Syria.
-Three cabinet sessions next week to discuss the 1997 budget.
-Minister of Culture and Higher Education Edde calls for the adoption of a new law for the preservation of ancient ruins.
-Minister of Transportation Miskawi: Lebanon encourages small investments.
-Lebanon's budget deficit was 47.8 percent in the first eight months of 1996, above the 38 percent target for the year.
-Some 409,955 voters in Bekaa to chose 21 deputies out of 142 candidates.
